title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 4

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the online briefing be held?
tasks.audioText: The college IT team is updating its guidance on protecting personal information. A short briefing will be held online on Wednesday at half past twelve. Students will learn how to create strong passwords, recognise suspicious messages and report a possible data leak. The link will be posted in the student portal on Tuesday afternoon.
options: On Wednesday at half past twelve
On Tuesday at half past twelve
On Wednesday at one thirty
On Thursday at half past twelve

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. When will the link be posted?
tasks.audioText: The college IT team is updating its guidance on protecting personal information. A short briefing will be held online on Wednesday at half past twelve. Students will learn how to create strong passwords, recognise suspicious messages and report a possible data leak. The link will be posted in the student portal on Tuesday afternoon.
options: On Friday
On Tuesday afternoon
Next month
After the event

tasks.prompt: A student received an email that appeared to come from the college IT department. It asked her to confirm her password using an unfamiliar link. She noticed that the sender's address was unusual and did not open the link. Instead, she forwarded the message to the official IT support address. The team confirmed that it was a phishing attempt and reminded students never to share passwords by email. Reading 1. What made the student suspicious?
options: The email contained a spelling mistake
The sender's address was unusual and the link was unfamiliar
The sender used the college logo incorrectly
The message included an unexpected attachment

tasks.prompt: What did the IT team confirm?
options: That the message was a routine college notice
That the message was a phishing attempt
That the student's password had already been changed
The message asked the student to update her timetable.

tasks.prompt: Students were advised ___ their passwords with anyone.
options: not to share
to not sharing
not share to
not shared

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO actions that improve account security.
options: Send passwords in an email
Reuse one password for every account
Use a unique strong password
Enable an additional verification step

tasks.prompt: A fraudulent message designed to steal personal information is a ___ attempt.
You receive a suspicious message asking for your login details. What should you do?
options: Reply with your password to check the sender.
Do not follow the link; report the message through the official channel.
Forward it to all your classmates.
Download every attachment.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of responsible technology use in a logical order.
options: Avoid the link and report the message
Notice an unexpected request
Follow the official security advice
Check the sender and message details
correctOrder: Check the sender and message details
Avoid the link and report the message

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words advising students how to protect personal information online. Include practical steps and explain why they matter.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: practical steps for protecting personal information are identified (0–2); the response explains why the steps matter and avoids unsafe or misleading security advice (0–2); recommendations are clearly organised with understandable grammar (0–2); privacy/digital-security vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
